description.summary: frames for windows that asked the compositor to decorate them

protocol.description: Clients that are not AppKit, such as foot, Qt, SDL or Wine, ask for server side decorations through xdg-decoration. The compositor does not draw those frames itself: it reports each such window to the one client that binds this global, the decorator, which renders the title strip with AppKit's own window frame code and hands it back as a buffer. The compositor shows the strip above the window, moves the window when the strip is dragged, and acts on the window buttons at the positions the decorator gave.

interface.name: pd_decorator_v1

description.summary: the decorator's view of the decorated windows

interface.description: Only one client may bind this global at a time, later binds are inert.

event.name: window
event.description: A new decorated window. The id stays valid until the removed event. Its state follows in title, width and active events, then done.

request.name: set_frame

description.summary: the title strip for a window

request.description: A buffer as wide as the last width event and height pixels tall, shown directly above the window. The buttons are three squares of the given size, their top edge at button_y in the strip, their left edges at close_x, mini_x and zoom_x. The compositor reads the buffer until the next set_frame for this id or the removed event, then releases it.
